title: Ok odd divisors even digits
statement: How many positive integers at most $300$ have an odd number of positive divisors and an even digit sum?
hints: When do the divisors of a number fail to pair up?
Pairing $d$ with $n/d$ shows only perfect squares qualify, so list the squares up to $300$ and check their digit sums.
solution: A positive integer has an odd number of divisors exactly when it is a perfect square, because divisors pair up as $d, n/d$ except when $d^2 = n$. The squares up to $300$ are $1^2, \dots, 17^2$. Their digit sums are $1,4,9,7,7,9,13,10,9,1,4,9,16,16,9,13,19$. The even ones belong to $4, 64, 121, 169, 196$, which gives $5$ numbers. Why this works. divisor-pairing: divisors pair up except at a square root, which leaves only squares.
check_program:
from sympy import divisor_count
print(sum(1 for n in range(1, 301) if divisor_count(n) % 2 == 1 and sum(map(int, str(n))) % 2 == 0))
